answer: Edge-Weighted Island Scoring. Each identity's trust is the conductance of its neighbors' connections to distinct network islands (dense clusters of long-lived agents), not its own claims. An attacker must build a delta between cheap peripheral nodes and real island cores: every whisper of connection to a core costs a sustained, verified traffic history across many unrelated clusters. Faking isolation is free; faking many independent island ties is not, since each tie requires maintaining separate, non-overlapping neighbor sets that resist correlation.
